content.$t:
HOPE

VA - Hope (A Butterboy Compilation) (4 x CDs)

When I began this project, I thought I was making a compilation about hope. The further I went, the more I realised that I first had to work out what hope actually means.

The word is everywhere. We hope things will improve... We hope tomorrow will be better... We hope everything will work out... But there is a danger in that version of hope. It can become passive. Something we feel while waiting for somebody else to change the world.

That wasn't the compilation I wanted to make. The idea that eventually became the DNA of these four CDs was simple, Hope requires action. Or, more bluntly, action delivers hope.

That changed my entire selection process.

This isn't a collection of songs that simply mention hope, optimism or a better future. Every track had to earn its place by contributing to a larger argument about what human beings can do when they refuse to become apathetic.

CD1 - Love, The Antidote to Apathy - begins with the most basic requirement, caring about other people. Love here isn't primarily romantic. It means compassion, friendship, empathy, responsibility and the willingness to see somebody else's suffering. It asks us to notice, to help and ultimately to change ourselves.

CD2 - The World as It Is - removes the comfortable distance. Before hope can have meaning, we have to look honestly at poverty, racism, war, exploitation, environmental destruction and political repression. These aren't abstract problems. They happen to real people. Hope cannot begin by looking away.

CD3 - Action - asks the unavoidable question, what are we going to do about it? This is where awareness becomes participation. The songs insist that ordinary people matter, that collective action matters, and that refusing to surrender is itself a form of resistance.

CD4 - The Future We Make - this is not the promise that everything will be all right. It is about rebuilding, reconciliation, responsibility, regeneration and protecting something worth saving. It asks what happens when hope becomes something we actually do.

The four CDs therefore form a journey: CARE → SEE → ACT → BUILD.

And the final track, Bob Marley & The Wailers' “Redemption Song,” is included so it leaves us with no easy escape. After listening to everything prior, the responsibility passes from the music to us.

I don't want this collection to leave you simply feeling inspired. I want it to make you think. Because perhaps hope isn't believing that someone will make the world better. 

Perhaps hope is deciding that you will help make it better yourself. (B)

This selection/pick sits right in the middle of a very specific corner of disco — the Salsoul Records world, which was its own thing even within the broader New York scene. Salsoul had its own DNA: Latin percussion, gospel-inflected vocals, lush orchestration, and a particular sense of drama that set it apart from the more stripped-down funk happening elsewhere. It's not the same universe as Patrick Adams, but there's definite overlap in spirit if not in sound — both were chasing something bigger and more emotional than the average dancefloor demanded. The label gave us some of the most beloved twelve-inch singles ever cut, and the remix culture around it — Gibbons, Pettibone — was as important as the records themselves. Thirteen tracks, no filler.

content.$t:
MINIMAL & BEAUTIFUL

VA - Bare‑Beautiful Universe (A Butterboy Compilation) (4 x CDs)

I hope you like Bare-Beautiful Universe, a four-disc journey into the spaces that music usually leaves untouched.

There are records that fill a room, and there are records that change the way a room feels. This collection belongs to the second kind. Its music is drawn towards restraint, intimacy and silence: voices that seem to arrive from the next room, guitars reduced to a few carefully chosen notes, pianos allowed to breathe between phrases, electronics that hover at the edge of hearing. Nothing here needs to shout for your attention.

Across four discs, the journey gradually turns inward.

CD1 - Falling Into Silence, begins with solitude. The world is still present, but increasingly distant, leaving the listener alone with a voice, a melody, a thought.

CD2 - Ghost-Tone Echoes, moves further away from the physical world. Drones, textures and slowly shifting sounds create a place where time seems to loosen and disappear.

CD3 - Bare-Soul Confessions, brings the human voice back to the centre. These are intimate songs, strange songs, vulnerable songs: music that feels less performed than revealed.

CD4 - Negative-Space Reveries, is where almost everything unnecessary has fallen away. What remains is fragile, skeletal and intensely human. A breath. A voice. A few notes. A memory suspended in silence.

That is the heart of Bare-Beautiful Universe.

This is not music designed to overwhelm you. It asks you to listen more closely. To notice the space between the notes, the hesitation in a voice, the sound that almost disappears before you have fully heard it.

Because silence is not the absence of music.  Sometimes, it is where the music lives.

Bare-Beautiful Universe is a sanctuary built from those moments, four discs for quiet rooms, late nights, solitary journeys and the rare occasions when we are willing to stop filling the silence and simply listen.

The universe is vast.  This one is deliberately small.  And within it, there is more than enough to hear. (B)
